From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & MAP request — draft checklist attached

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. I've pulled together a short cost-validation checklist and attached a living MAP spreadsheet (MAP-AcmeHealth-v1.xlsx). Below are the headline assumptions and the conservative/optimistic cost lines. If these look right I will finalize the MAP and route to procurement + legal.

Headline assumptions (please confirm):
- Avg tokens per user request: 750 tokens
- Requests/day (pilot): 200 active sessions -> ~150,000 tokens/day
- Target latency SLO (p99): 250ms
- Quantization: Q4_0 recommended for production pilot; Q8 if you want higher throughput at slight quality regression
- Caching: template/prefix caching expected hit rate 25% (templates + KV cache)
- Batching: dynamic batching with target batch size 8; max batch 16; batching timeout 30ms

Preliminary cost lines (hosted API nominal rates, + caching/batching uplift):
- Base nominal hosted rate: $0.0023 / 1k tokens (note: we price per 1k tokens on platform)
- Conservative effective unit cost (minimal caching/batching): $0.0018 / 1k tokens
- Expected effective unit cost (with 25% cache hit + batching savings): $0.0009 / 1k tokens

Estimates for 90-day pilot (150k tokens/day):
- Conservative (low caching, conservative batching): 150k * 90 days * $0.0018 = $24,300
- Expected (25% cache hit, recommended batching): 150k * 90 days * $0.0009 = $12,150

Notes on latency tradeoffs: dynamic batching improves cost by ~35% at our observed distributions but can add 30–80ms extra tail latency depending on peak traffic. With your 250ms p99 target, I recommend keeping max batch at 16 and a 30ms timeout for the pilot; we can tighten later.

Attached: MAP-AcmeHealth-v1.xlsx (draft mutual action plan) — contains a cost sensitivity tab, rollout timeline, evaluation plan, and procurement checklist. Also included a short procurement cheatsheet in the drive link.

Next steps: please confirm the session/day assumption and whether 250ms p99 is acceptable. Once you confirm we'll run a quick internal perf sweep under similar workload and then I will send a finalized MAP for procurement and legal.

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

On Fri, Oct 1, 2026 at 11:03 AM Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached: MAP-AcmeHealth-v1.xlsx (draft mutual action plan) — contains a cost sensitivity tab, rollout timeline, evaluation plan, and procurement checklist.

Quick technical validation — copying the key points here so procurement has the right language in the MAP: 
- Memory/throughput: for a 750-token average prompt, a single A100-80GB can sustain ~1100 tokens/sec under Q4_0 in our runtime with KV-enabled caching. That maps to ~95 rps (requests/sec) if batching is used effectively.
- Quantization tradeoffs: Q4_0 gives near native quality with ~2.3x throughput vs fp16. Q8 increases throughput another ~1.3x but increases hallucination risk slightly for sensitive instructions — callout in MAP.
- Batching impact: observed token-level cost reduction 20–40% depending on batch-size distribution; P99 latency increased by 40–70ms at larger batch limits. Recommend default batch_target=8, batch_max=16, batch_wait=30ms for pilot.
- Caching guidance: prefix/KV caching is policy-driven. For templated prompts we recommend conservative hit-rate 30% initially; include a column in the MAP to capture expected hit rate per flow.

I'll run a quick internal benchmark (1K sample prompts representative of Acme's templates) and post results to the drive. Attaching a draft sensitivity chart for the MAP: cost_sensitivity_chart.png

If procurement asks for an SLA-backed route to dedicated capacity, note that Dedicated pricing numbers will be in the MAP appendix (monthly committed vs on-demand effective unit cost). We should include a fallback policy to a cheaper model for low-risk/analytics queries to keep costs predictable.

— Priyom
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
